14.web: Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
14.kjv: Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of his grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
14.bsb: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.

14.web: But the multitude of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
14.kjv: But the multitude of the city was divided: and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
14.bsb: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.

14.web: When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone them,
14.kjv: And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews with their rulers, to use them despitefully, and to stone them,
14.bsb: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,

14.web: they became aware of it, and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.
14.kjv: They were ware of it , and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lieth round about:
14.bsb: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,

14.web: There they preached the Good News.
14.kjv: And there they preached the gospel.
14.bsb: where they continued to preach the gospel.

14.web: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.
14.kjv: And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked:
14.bsb: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.

14.web: He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
14.kjv: The same heard Paul speak: who stedfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,
14.bsb: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.

14.web: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.
14.kjv: Said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.
14.bsb: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.

14.web: When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
14.kjv: And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
14.bsb: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”

14.web: They called Barnabas “Jupiter”, and Paul “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.
14.kjv: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.
14.bsb: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.

14.web: The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have made a sacrifice along with the multitudes.
14.kjv: Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people.
14.bsb: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.

14.web: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they tore their clothes, and sprang into the multitude, crying out,
14.kjv: Which when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of , they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,
14.bsb: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,

14.web: “Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;
14.kjv: And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein:
14.bsb: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

14.web: who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.
14.kjv: Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
14.bsb: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.

14.web: Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”
14.kjv: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
14.bsb: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

14.web: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the multitudes from making a sacrifice to them.
14.kjv: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the people, that they had not done sacrifice unto them.
14.bsb: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.

14.web: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
14.kjv: And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.
14.bsb: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.

14.web: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
14.kjv: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
14.bsb: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.

14.web: When they had preached the Good News to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
14.kjv: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,
14.bsb: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

14.web: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.
14.kjv: Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.
14.bsb: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.

14.web: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.
14.kjv: And when they had ordained them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed.
14.bsb: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

14.web: They passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.
14.kjv: And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
14.bsb: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

14.web: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
14.kjv: And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia:
14.bsb: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

14.web: From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
14.kjv: And thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.
14.bsb: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.

14.web: When they had arrived, and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
14.kjv: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all that God had done with them, and how he had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles.
14.bsb: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

14.web: They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.
14.kjv: And there they abode long time with the disciples.
14.bsb: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.

15.web: Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised after the custom of Moses, you can’t be saved.”
15.kjv: And certain men which came down from Judæa taught the brethren, and said , Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
15.bsb: Then some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”

15.web: Therefore when Paul and Barnabas had no small discord and discussion with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas, and some others of them, to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.
15.kjv: When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
15.bsb: And after engaging these men in sharp debate, Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.

15.web: They, being sent on their way by the assembly, passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles. They caused great joy to all the brothers.
15.kjv: And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.
15.bsb: Sent on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.

15.web: When they had come to Jerusalem, they were received by the assembly and the apostles and the elders, and they reported all things that God had done with them.
15.kjv: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.
15.bsb: On their arrival in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and apostles and elders, to whom they reported all that God had done through them.

15.web: But some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.”
15.kjv: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
15.bsb: But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared, “The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses.”

15.web: The apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this matter.
15.kjv: And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.
15.bsb: So the apostles and elders met to look into this matter.

15.web: When there had been much discussion, Peter rose up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that a good while ago God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the nations should hear the word of the Good News, and believe.
15.kjv: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
15.bsb: After much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you that the Gentiles would hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.

15.web: God, who knows the heart, testified about them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just like he did to us.
15.kjv: And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
15.bsb: And God, who knows the heart, showed His approval by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as He did to us.

15.web: He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
15.kjv: And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
15.bsb: He made no distinction between us and them, for He cleansed their hearts by faith.

15.web: Now therefore why do you tempt God, that you should put a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
15.kjv: Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
15.bsb: Now then, why do you test God by placing on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?

15.web: But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.”
15.kjv: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.
15.bsb: On the contrary, we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”

15.web: All the multitude kept silence, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul reporting what signs and wonders God had done among the nations through them.
15.kjv: Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them.
15.bsb: The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

15.web: After they were silent, James answered, “Brothers, listen to me.
15.kjv: And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me:
15.bsb: When they had finished speaking, James declared, “Brothers, listen to me!

15.web: Simeon has reported how God first visited the nations, to take out of them a people for his name.
15.kjv: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.
15.bsb: Simon has told us how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people to be His own.

15.web: This agrees with the words of the prophets. As it is written,
15.kjv: And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written,
15.bsb: The words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written:

15.web: ‘After these things I will return. I will again build the tabernacle of David, which has fallen. I will again build its ruins. I will set it up,
15.kjv: After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up:
15.bsb: ‘After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,

15.web: That the rest of men may seek after the Lord; all the Gentiles who are called by my name, says the Lord, who does all these things.
15.kjv: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.
15.bsb: so that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord who does these things

15.web: All of God’s works are known to him from eternity.’
15.kjv: Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.
15.bsb: that have been known for ages.’

15.web: “Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,
15.kjv: Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God:
15.bsb: It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not cause trouble for the Gentiles who are turning to God.

15.web: but that we write to them that they abstain from the pollution of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.
15.kjv: But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.
15.bsb: Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.

15.web: For Moses from generations of old has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”
15.kjv: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.
15.bsb: For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”

15.web: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole assembly, to choose men out of their company, and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers.
15.kjv: Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely , Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
15.bsb: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,

15.web: They wrote these things by their hand: “The apostles, the elders, and the brothers, to the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.
15.kjv: And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia:
15.bsb: and sent them with this letter: The apostles and the elders, your brothers, To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.

15.web: Because we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying, ‘You must be circumcised and keep the law,’ to whom we gave no commandment;
15.kjv: Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment:
15.bsb: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.

15.web: it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose out men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
15.kjv: It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
15.bsb: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

15.web: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
15.kjv: Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
15.bsb: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

15.web: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who themselves will also tell you the same things by word of mouth.
15.kjv: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.
15.bsb: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.

15.web: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay no greater burden on you than these necessary things:
15.kjv: For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;
15.bsb: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:

15.web: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality, from which if you keep yourselves, it will be well with you. Farewell.”
15.kjv: That ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication: from which if ye keep yourselves, ye shall do well. Fare ye well.
15.bsb: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.

15.web: So, when they were sent off, they came to Antioch. Having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
15.kjv: So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle:
15.bsb: So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.

15.web: When they had read it, they rejoiced over the encouragement.
15.kjv: Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.
15.bsb: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.

15.web: Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves, encouraged the brothers with many words, and strengthened them.
15.kjv: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them .
15.bsb: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.

15.web: After they had spent some time there, they were sent back with greetings from the brothers to the apostles.
15.kjv: And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.
15.bsb: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.

15.kjv: Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.

15.web: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
15.kjv: Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
15.bsb: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.

15.web: After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s return now and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
15.kjv: And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.
15.bsb: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”

15.web: Barnabas planned to take John, who was called Mark, with them also.
15.kjv: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.
15.bsb: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.

15.web: But Paul didn’t think that it was a good idea to take with them someone who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia, and didn’t go with them to do the work.
15.kjv: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
15.bsb: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.

15.web: Then the contention grew so sharp that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark with him, and sailed away to Cyprus,
15.kjv: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
15.bsb: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,

15.web: but Paul chose Silas, and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of God.
15.kjv: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.
15.bsb: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

15.web: He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.
15.kjv: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
15.bsb: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

16.web: He came to Derbe and Lystra: and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed; but his father was a Greek.
16.kjv: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
16.bsb: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.

16.web: The brothers who were at Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.
16.kjv: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
16.bsb: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.

16.web: Paul wanted to have him go out with him, and he took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those parts; for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
16.kjv: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
16.bsb: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

16.web: As they went on their way through the cities, they delivered the decrees to them to keep which had been ordained by the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.
16.kjv: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.
16.bsb: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.

16.web: So the assemblies were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily.
16.kjv: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
16.bsb: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.

16.web: When they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.
16.kjv: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,
16.bsb: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.

16.web: When they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn’t allow them.
16.kjv: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.
16.bsb: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.

16.web: Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
16.kjv: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.
16.bsb: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

16.web: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him, and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”
16.kjv: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
16.bsb: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”

16.web: When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.
16.kjv: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.
16.bsb: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

16.web: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;
16.kjv: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
16.bsb: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.

16.web: and from there to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony. We were staying some days in this city.
16.kjv: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
16.bsb: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.

16.web: On the Sabbath day we went outside of the city by a riverside, where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and we sat down, and spoke to the women who had come together.
16.kjv: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.
16.bsb: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.

16.web: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us; whose heart the Lord opened to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.
16.kjv: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us : whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
16.bsb: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.

16.web: When she and her household were baptized, she begged us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and stay.” So she persuaded us.
16.kjv: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us , saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there . And she constrained us.
16.bsb: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.

16.web: As we were going to prayer, a certain girl having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by fortune telling.
16.kjv: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:
16.bsb: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.

16.web: Following Paul and us, she cried out, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation!”
16.kjv: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.
16.bsb: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”

16.web: She was doing this for many days. But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!” It came out that very hour.
16.kjv: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
16.bsb: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.

16.web: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas, and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
16.kjv: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,
16.bsb: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.

16.web: When they had brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Jews, are agitating our city,
16.kjv: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
16.bsb: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil

16.web: and advocate customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans.”
16.kjv: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
16.bsb: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”

16.web: The multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates tore their clothes from them, and commanded them to be beaten with rods.
16.kjv: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them .
16.bsb: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.

16.web: When they had laid many stripes on them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely,
16.kjv: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
16.bsb: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.

16.web: who, having received such a command, threw them into the inner prison, and secured their feet in the stocks.
16.kjv: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
16.bsb: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.

16.web: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
16.kjv: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
16.bsb: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

16.web: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.
16.kjv: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
16.bsb: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.

16.web: The jailer, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
16.kjv: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
16.bsb: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.

16.web: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”
16.kjv: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
16.bsb: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”

16.web: He called for lights, sprang in, fell down trembling before Paul and Silas,
16.kjv: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
16.bsb: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

16.web: brought them out, and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
16.kjv: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
16.bsb: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

16.web: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
16.kjv: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
16.bsb: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”

16.web: They spoke the word of the Lord to him, and to all who were in his house.
16.kjv: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
16.bsb: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.

16.web: He took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes, and was immediately baptized, he and all his household.
16.kjv: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
16.bsb: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.

16.web: He brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his household, having believed in God.
16.kjv: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
16.bsb: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.

16.web: But when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, “Let those men go.”
16.kjv: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
16.bsb: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”

16.web: The jailer reported these words to Paul, saying, “The magistrates have sent to let you go; now therefore come out, and go in peace.”
16.kjv: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
16.bsb: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”

16.web: But Paul said to them, “They have beaten us publicly, without a trial, men who are Romans, and have cast us into prison! Do they now release us secretly? No, most certainly, but let them come themselves and bring us out!”
16.kjv: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
16.bsb: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”

16.web: The sergeants reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans,
16.kjv: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
16.bsb: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.

16.web: and they came and begged them. When they had brought them out, they asked them to depart from the city.
16.kjv: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
16.bsb: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.

16.web: They went out of the prison, and entered into Lydia’s house. When they had seen the brothers, they encouraged them, and departed.
16.kjv: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
16.bsb: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.

17.web: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
17.kjv: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
17.bsb: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

17.web: Paul, as was his custom, went in to them, and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
17.kjv: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
17.bsb: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

17.web: explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus, whom I proclaim to you, is the Christ.”
17.kjv: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.
17.bsb: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.

17.web: Some of them were persuaded, and joined Paul and Silas, of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and not a few of the chief women.
17.kjv: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
17.bsb: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.

17.web: But the unpersuaded Jews took along some wicked men from the marketplace, and gathering a crowd, set the city in an uproar. Assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.
17.kjv: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
17.bsb: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.

17.web: When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city, crying, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here also,
17.kjv: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
17.bsb: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,

17.web: whom Jason has received. These all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus!”
17.kjv: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cæsar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
17.bsb: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”

17.web: The multitude and the rulers of the city were troubled when they heard these things.
17.kjv: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
17.bsb: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.

17.web: When they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
17.kjv: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
17.bsb: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.

17.web: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
17.kjv: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
17.bsb: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

17.web: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.
17.kjv: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
17.bsb: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.

17.web: Many of them therefore believed; also of the prominent Greek women, and not a few men.
17.kjv: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
17.bsb: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.

17.web: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul at Beroea also, they came there likewise, agitating the multitudes.
17.kjv: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
17.bsb: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.

17.web: Then the brothers immediately sent out Paul to go as far as to the sea, and Silas and Timothy still stayed there.
17.kjv: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
17.bsb: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.

17.web: But those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens. Receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him very quickly, they departed.
17.kjv: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
17.bsb: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.

17.web: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.
17.kjv: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
17.bsb: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.

17.web: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.
17.kjv: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
17.bsb: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.

17.web: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were conversing with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign deities,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.
17.kjv: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
17.bsb: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.

17.web: They took hold of him, and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is, which is spoken by you?
17.kjv: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is ?
17.bsb: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?

17.web: For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We want to know therefore what these things mean.”
17.kjv: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
17.bsb: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”

17.web: Now all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.
17.kjv: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
17.bsb: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.

17.web: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus, and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.
17.kjv: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
17.bsb: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.

17.web: For as I passed along, and observed the objects of your worship, I found also an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, this I announce to you.
17.kjv: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
17.bsb: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.

17.web: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands,
17.kjv: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
17.bsb: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.

17.web: neither is he served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.
17.kjv: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
17.bsb: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

17.web: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons, and the boundaries of their dwellings,
17.kjv: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
17.bsb: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.

17.web: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.
17.kjv: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
17.bsb: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

17.web: ‘For in him we live, and move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’
17.kjv: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
17.bsb: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’

17.web: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art and design of man.
17.kjv: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.
17.bsb: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.

17.web: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked. But now he commands that all people everywhere should repent,
17.kjv: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
17.bsb: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.

17.web: because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.”
17.kjv: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men , in that he hath raised him from the dead.
17.bsb: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”

17.web: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, “We want to hear you again concerning this.”
17.kjv: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter .
17.bsb: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”

17.web: Thus Paul went out from among them.
17.kjv: So Paul departed from among them.
17.bsb: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.

17.web: But certain men joined with him, and believed, among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
17.kjv: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
17.bsb: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.

18.web: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.
18.kjv: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
18.bsb: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

18.web: He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,
18.kjv: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
18.bsb: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,

18.web: and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.
18.kjv: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
18.bsb: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.

18.web: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded Jews and Greeks.
18.kjv: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
18.bsb: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.

18.web: But when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
18.kjv: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
18.bsb: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

18.web: When they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his clothing and said to them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am clean. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles!”
18.kjv: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
18.bsb: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

18.web: He departed there, and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.
18.kjv: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
18.bsb: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

18.web: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.
18.kjv: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
18.bsb: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.

18.web: The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, “Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;
18.kjv: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
18.bsb: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.

18.web: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”
18.kjv: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
18.bsb: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”

18.web: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
18.kjv: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
18.bsb: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.

18.web: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,
18.kjv: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
18.bsb: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

18.web: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”
18.kjv: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
18.bsb: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.

18.web: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;
18.kjv: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
18.bsb: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.

18.web: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”
18.kjv: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it ; for I will be no judge of such matters .
18.bsb: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”

18.web: So he drove them from the judgment seat.
18.kjv: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
18.bsb: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.

18.web: Then all the Greeks laid hold on Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.
18.kjv: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
18.bsb: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.

18.web: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
18.kjv: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
18.bsb: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.

18.web: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
18.kjv: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
18.bsb: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.

18.web: When they asked him to stay with them a longer time, he declined;
18.kjv: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
18.bsb: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.

18.web: but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.
18.kjv: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
18.bsb: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.

18.web: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.
18.kjv: And when he had landed at Cæsarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
18.bsb: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.

18.web: Having spent some time there, he departed, and went through the region of Galatia, and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
18.kjv: And after he had spent some time there , he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
18.bsb: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

18.web: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.
18.kjv: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
18.bsb: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.

18.web: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.
18.kjv: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
18.bsb: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.

18.web: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
18.kjv: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them , and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
18.bsb: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

18.web: When he had determined to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him, and wrote to the disciples to receive him. When he had come, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace;
18.kjv: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
18.bsb: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.

18.web: for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
18.kjv: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
18.bsb: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

19.web: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples.
19.kjv: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
19.bsb: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples

19.web: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
19.kjv: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
19.bsb: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

19.web: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”
19.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.
19.bsb: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.

19.web: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Jesus.”
19.kjv: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
19.bsb: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”

19.web: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
19.kjv: When they heard this , they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
19.bsb: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

19.web: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.
19.kjv: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
19.bsb: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.

19.web: They were about twelve men in all.
19.kjv: And all the men were about twelve.
19.bsb: There were about twelve men in all.

19.web: He entered into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.
19.kjv: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
19.bsb: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.

19.web: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
19.kjv: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
19.bsb: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

19.web: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
19.kjv: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
19.bsb: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.

19.web: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,
19.kjv: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
19.bsb: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,

19.web: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
19.kjv: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
19.bsb: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.

19.web: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”
19.kjv: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
19.bsb: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I bind you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”

19.web: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.
19.kjv: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
19.bsb: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

19.web: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”
19.kjv: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
19.bsb: Eventually, one of the evil spirits answered them, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”

19.web: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
19.kjv: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
19.bsb: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.

19.web: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
19.kjv: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
19.bsb: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.

19.web: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.
19.kjv: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
19.bsb: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.

19.web: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
19.kjv: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men : and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
19.bsb: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.

19.web: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.
19.kjv: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
19.bsb: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.

19.web: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”
19.kjv: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
19.bsb: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”

19.web: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
19.kjv: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
19.bsb: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.

19.web: About that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.
19.kjv: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
19.bsb: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.

19.web: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,
19.kjv: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
19.bsb: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen.

19.web: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.
19.kjv: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
19.bsb: Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades. “Men,” he said, “you know that this business is our source of prosperity.

19.web: You see and hear, that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands.
19.kjv: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
19.bsb: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.

19.web: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”
19.kjv: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
19.bsb: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed—she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”

19.web: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.kjv: And when they heard these sayings , they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
19.bsb: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

19.web: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.
19.kjv: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
19.bsb: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.

19.web: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.
19.kjv: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
