19.bsb: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.

19.web: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.
19.kjv: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
19.bsb: Even some of Paul’s friends who were officials of the province of Asia sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.

19.web: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.
19.kjv: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
19.bsb: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.

19.web: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.
19.kjv: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
19.bsb: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward to explain himself, and he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people.

19.web: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.kjv: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
19.bsb: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

19.web: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?
19.kjv: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
19.bsb: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?

19.web: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.
19.kjv: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
19.bsb: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.

19.web: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.
19.kjv: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
19.bsb: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess.

19.web: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.
19.kjv: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
19.bsb: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.

19.web: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.
19.kjv: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
19.bsb: But if you are seeking anything beyond this, it must be settled in a legal assembly.

19.web: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”
19.kjv: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
19.bsb: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”

19.web: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
19.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
19.bsb: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.

20.web: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
20.kjv: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them , and departed for to go into Macedonia.
20.bsb: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

20.web: When he had gone through those parts, and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.
20.kjv: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
20.bsb: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,

20.web: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
20.kjv: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
20.bsb: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.

20.web: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea; Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians; Gaius of Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
20.kjv: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
20.bsb: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.

20.web: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.
20.kjv: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
20.bsb: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.

20.web: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
20.kjv: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
20.bsb: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.

20.web: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day, and continued his speech until midnight.
20.kjv: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
20.bsb: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.

20.web: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.
20.kjv: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
20.bsb: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

20.web: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor, and was taken up dead.
20.kjv: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
20.bsb: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.

20.web: Paul went down, and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”
20.kjv: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
20.bsb: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”

20.web: When he had gone up, and had broken bread, and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.
20.kjv: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
20.bsb: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.

20.web: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.
20.kjv: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
20.bsb: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.

20.web: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.
20.kjv: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
20.bsb: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.

20.web: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard, and came to Mitylene.
20.kjv: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
20.bsb: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.

20.web: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.
20.kjv: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
20.bsb: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.

20.web: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
20.kjv: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
20.bsb: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

20.web: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
20.kjv: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
20.bsb: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

20.web: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,
20.kjv: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
20.bsb: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.

20.web: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;
20.kjv: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
20.bsb: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.

20.web: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,
20.kjv: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you , but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
20.bsb: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,

20.web: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus.
20.kjv: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
20.bsb: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.

20.web: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;
20.kjv: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
20.bsb: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.

20.web: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.
20.kjv: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
20.bsb: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.

20.web: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
20.kjv: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
20.bsb: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.

20.web: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.
20.kjv: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
20.bsb: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.

20.web: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,
20.kjv: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men .
20.bsb: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.

20.web: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
20.kjv: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
20.bsb: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.

20.web: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves, and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.
20.kjv: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
20.bsb: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.

20.web: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
20.kjv: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
20.bsb: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.

20.web: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
20.kjv: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
20.bsb: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.

20.web: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.
20.kjv: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
20.bsb: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.

20.web: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up, and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
20.kjv: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
20.bsb: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.

20.web: I coveted no one’s silver, or gold, or clothing.
20.kjv: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
20.bsb: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.

20.web: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.
20.kjv: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
20.bsb: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

20.web: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
20.kjv: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
20.bsb: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

20.web: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
20.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
20.bsb: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

20.web: They all wept a lot, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,
20.kjv: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
20.bsb: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

20.web: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.
20.kjv: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
20.bsb: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

21.web: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
21.kjv: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
21.bsb: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

21.web: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set sail.
21.kjv: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
21.bsb: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.

21.web: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria, and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload her cargo.
21.kjv: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
21.bsb: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

21.web: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
21.kjv: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
21.bsb: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

21.web: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
21.kjv: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
21.bsb: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.

21.web: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
21.kjv: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
21.bsb: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.

21.web: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers, and stayed with them one day.
21.kjv: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
21.bsb: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.

21.web: On the next day, we, who were Paul’s companions, departed, and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.
21.kjv: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
21.bsb: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.

21.web: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
21.kjv: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
21.bsb: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

21.web: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
21.kjv: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.
21.bsb: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

21.web: Coming to us, and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “Thus says the Holy Spirit: ‘So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
21.kjv: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
21.bsb: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’”

21.web: When we heard these things, both we and they of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.kjv: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.bsb: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

21.web: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
21.kjv: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
21.bsb: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

21.web: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”
21.kjv: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
21.bsb: When he would not be dissuaded, we fell silent and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”

21.web: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.
21.kjv: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
21.bsb: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.

21.web: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.
21.kjv: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cæsarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
21.bsb: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple.

21.web: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
21.kjv: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
21.bsb: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.

21.web: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.
21.kjv: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
21.bsb: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.

21.web: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.
21.kjv: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
21.bsb: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

21.web: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.
21.kjv: And when they heard it , they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
21.bsb: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.

21.web: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children neither to walk after the customs.
21.kjv: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
21.bsb: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.

21.web: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.
21.kjv: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
21.bsb: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.

21.web: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.
21.kjv: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
21.bsb: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.

21.web: Take them, and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.
21.kjv: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
21.bsb: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.

21.web: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”
21.kjv: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
21.bsb: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”

21.web: Then Paul took the men, and the next day, purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.
21.kjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
21.bsb: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them.

21.web: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
21.kjv: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
21.bsb: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,

21.web: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple, and has defiled this holy place!”
21.kjv: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
21.bsb: crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”

21.web: For they had seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
21.kjv: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
21.bsb: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

21.web: All the city was moved, and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.
21.kjv: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
21.bsb: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.

21.web: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
21.kjv: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
21.bsb: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.

21.web: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.
21.kjv: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
21.bsb: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

21.web: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.
21.kjv: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
21.bsb: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.

21.web: Some shouted one thing, and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.
21.kjv: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
21.bsb: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.

21.web: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
21.kjv: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
21.bsb: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.

21.web: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”
21.kjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
21.bsb: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!”

21.web: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?
21.kjv: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
21.bsb: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?” “Do you speak Greek?” he replied.

21.web: Aren’t you then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”
21.kjv: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
21.bsb: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the ‘Assassins’ into the wilderness?”

21.web: But Paul said, “I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”
21.kjv: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
21.bsb: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”

21.web: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
21.kjv: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
21.bsb: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:

22.web: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”
22.kjv: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.
22.bsb: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”

22.web: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,
22.kjv: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
22.bsb: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent. Then Paul declared,

22.web: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.
22.kjv: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
22.bsb: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I am just as zealous for God as any of you here today.

22.web: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
22.kjv: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
22.bsb: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,

22.web: As also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.
22.kjv: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
22.bsb: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.

22.web: As I made my journey, and came close to Damascus, about noon, suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.
22.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
22.bsb: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.

22.web: I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
22.kjv: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
22.bsb: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’

22.web: I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’
22.kjv: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
22.bsb: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.

22.web: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.
22.kjv: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
22.bsb: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.

22.web: I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’
22.kjv: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
22.bsb: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’

22.web: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
22.kjv: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
22.bsb: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.

22.web: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,
22.kjv: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there ,
22.bsb: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,

22.web: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.
22.kjv: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
22.bsb: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.

22.web: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.
22.kjv: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
22.bsb: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear His voice.

22.web: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
22.kjv: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
22.bsb: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.

22.web: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’
22.kjv: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
22.bsb: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’

22.web: “When I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,
22.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
22.bsb: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance

22.web: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’
22.kjv: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
22.bsb: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’

22.web: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.
22.kjv: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
22.bsb: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.

22.web: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’
22.kjv: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
22.bsb: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’

22.web: “He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’”
22.kjv: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
22.bsb: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”

22.web: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice, and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”
22.kjv: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
22.bsb: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”

22.web: As they cried out, and threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,
22.kjv: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
22.bsb: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,

22.web: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.
22.kjv: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
22.bsb: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.

22.web: When they had tied him up with thongs, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”
22.kjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
22.bsb: But as they stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”

22.web: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”
22.kjv: When the centurion heard that , he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
22.bsb: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “What are you going to do?” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”

22.web: The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”
22.kjv: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
22.bsb: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” he answered.

22.web: The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.” Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”
22.kjv: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
22.bsb: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander. “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.

22.web: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.
22.kjv: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
22.bsb: Then those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.

22.web: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
22.kjv: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
22.bsb: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.

23.web: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”
23.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
23.bsb: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin and said, “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”

23.web: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
23.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
23.bsb: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

23.web: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
23.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
23.bsb: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”

23.web: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
23.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
23.bsb: But those standing nearby said, “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”

23.web: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”
23.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
23.bsb: “Brothers,” Paul replied, “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’”

23.web: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
23.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
23.bsb: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”

23.web: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.
23.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
23.bsb: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

23.web: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.
23.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
23.bsb: For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection, nor angels, nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.

23.web: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”
23.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
23.bsb: A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”

23.web: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.
23.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
23.bsb: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.

23.web: The following night, the Lord stood by him, and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”
23.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
23.bsb: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”

23.web: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
23.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
23.bsb: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

23.web: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.
23.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
23.bsb: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.

23.web: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
23.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
23.bsb: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.

23.web: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
23.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
23.bsb: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”

23.web: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.
23.kjv: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
23.bsb: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.

23.web: Paul summoned one of the centurions, and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”
23.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him , and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
23.bsb: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”

23.web: So he took him, and brought him to the commanding officer, and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to tell you.”
23.kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him , and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
23.bsb: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

23.web: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”
23.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him , What is that thou hast to tell me?
23.bsb: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”

23.web: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
23.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
23.bsb: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.

23.web: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”
23.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
23.bsb: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”

23.web: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”
23.kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
23.bsb: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”

23.web: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen, and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”
23.kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
23.bsb: Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.

23.web: He asked them to provide animals, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
23.kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
23.bsb: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”

23.web: He wrote a letter like this:
23.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
23.bsb: And he wrote the following letter:

23.web: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
23.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
23.bsb: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.

23.web: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them, when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
23.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
23.bsb: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,

23.web: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.
23.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
23.bsb: and since I wanted to understand their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.

23.web: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.
23.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
23.bsb: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.

23.web: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”
23.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
23.bsb: When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you.

23.web: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
23.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
23.bsb: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.

23.web: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.
23.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
23.bsb: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.

23.web: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
23.kjv: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
23.bsb: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.

23.web: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,
23.kjv: And when the governor had read the letter , he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
23.bsb: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,

23.web: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
23.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
23.bsb: he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.

24.web: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.
24.kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
24.bsb: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.

24.web: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,
24.kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him , saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
24.bsb: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation.

24.web: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
24.kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
24.bsb: In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.

24.web: But, that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.
24.kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
24.bsb: But in order not to burden you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.

24.web: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
24.kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow , and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
24.bsb: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,

24.web: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.
24.kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
24.bsb: and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.

24.kjv: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us , and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

24.web: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”
24.kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
24.bsb: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”

24.web: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.
24.kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
24.bsb: The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true.

24.web: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,
24.kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
24.bsb: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.

24.web: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.
24.kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
24.bsb: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

24.web: In the temple they didn’t find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues, or in the city.
24.kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
24.bsb: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.

24.web: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
24.kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
24.bsb: Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.

24.web: But this I confess to you, that after the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;
24.kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
24.bsb: I do confess to you, however, that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets,

24.web: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
24.kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
24.bsb: and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

24.web: Herein I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.
24.kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
24.bsb: In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.

24.web: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;
24.kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
24.bsb: After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.

24.web: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.
24.kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
24.bsb: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia

24.web: They ought to have been here before you, and to make accusation, if they had anything against me.
24.kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
24.bsb: who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.

24.web: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,
24.kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
24.bsb: Otherwise, let these men state for themselves any crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin,

24.web: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”
24.kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
24.bsb: unless it was this one thing I called out as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’”

24.web: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, “When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.”
24.kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
24.bsb: Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”

24.web: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody, and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.
24.kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
24.bsb: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to minister to his needs.

24.web: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla, his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
24.kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
24.bsb: After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

24.web: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, “Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.”
24.kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
24.bsb: As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”

24.web: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often, and talked with him.
24.kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
24.bsb: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe. So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.

24.web: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.
24.kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
24.bsb: After two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.

25.web: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
25.kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.
25.bsb: Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,

25.web: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,
25.kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
25.bsb: where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus

25.web: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem; plotting to kill him on the way.
25.kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
25.bsb: to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.

25.web: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.
25.kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither .
25.bsb: But Festus replied, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.

25.web: “Let them therefore”, said he, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”
25.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me , and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
25.bsb: So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”

25.web: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.
25.kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
25.bsb: After spending no more than eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in.

25.web: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,
25.kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
25.bsb: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.

25.web: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”
25.kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.
25.bsb: Then Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”

25.web: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem, and be judged by me there concerning these things?”
25.kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
25.bsb: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”

25.web: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.
25.kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
25.bsb: Paul replied, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

25.web: For if I have done wrong, and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
25.kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
25.bsb: If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

25.web: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”
25.kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.
25.bsb: Then Festus conferred with his council and replied, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”

25.web: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, and greeted Festus.
25.kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.
25.bsb: After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

25.web: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;
