25.kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
25.bsb: Since they were staying several days, Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.

25.web: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.
25.kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me , desiring to have judgment against him.
25.bsb: While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.

25.web: To whom I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction, before the accused has met the accusers face to face, and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.
25.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
25.bsb: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.

25.web: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought.
25.kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
25.bsb: So when they came here with me, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.

25.web: Concerning whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such things as I supposed;
25.kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
25.bsb: But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.

25.web: but had certain questions against him about their own religion, and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
25.kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
25.bsb: They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

25.web: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.
25.kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
25.bsb: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.

25.web: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”
25.kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.
25.bsb: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”

25.web: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”
25.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
25.bsb: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.

25.web: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
25.kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.
25.bsb: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.

25.web: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
25.kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
25.bsb: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.

25.web: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him,
25.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
25.bsb: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.

25.web: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination, I may have something to write.
25.kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
25.bsb: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign one about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.

25.web: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”
25.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
25.bsb: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”

26.web: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
26.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
26.bsb: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:

26.web: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,
26.kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
26.bsb: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,

26.web: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
26.kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
26.bsb: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.

26.web: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;
26.kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
26.bsb: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from the earliest days of my youth, among my own people and in Jerusalem.

26.web: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
26.kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
26.bsb: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.

26.web: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
26.kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
26.bsb: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,

26.web: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!
26.kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
26.bsb: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to realize as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.

26.web: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?
26.kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
26.bsb: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

26.web: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
26.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
26.bsb: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

26.web: This I also did in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
26.kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them .
26.bsb: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.

26.web: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
26.kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
26.bsb: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.

26.web: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,
26.kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
26.bsb: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

26.web: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.
26.kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
26.bsb: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.

26.web: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
26.kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
26.bsb: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

26.web: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
26.kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
26.bsb: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.

26.web: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen, and of the things which I will reveal to you;
26.kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
26.bsb: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.

26.web: delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,
26.kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
26.bsb: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them

26.web: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
26.kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
26.bsb: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’

26.web: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
26.kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
26.bsb: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

26.web: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
26.kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
26.bsb: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.

26.web: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple, and tried to kill me.
26.kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me .
26.bsb: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.

26.web: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,
26.kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
26.bsb: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:

26.web: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”
26.kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
26.bsb: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”

26.web: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”
26.kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
26.bsb: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”

26.web: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.
26.kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
26.bsb: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.

26.web: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
26.kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
26.bsb: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

26.web: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
26.kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
26.bsb: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”

26.web: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”
26.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
26.bsb: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”

26.web: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”
26.kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
26.bsb: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”

26.web: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them.
26.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
26.bsb: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.

26.web: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
26.kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
26.bsb: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”

26.web: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
26.kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
26.bsb: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

27.web: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
27.kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
27.bsb: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.

27.web: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
27.kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
27.bsb: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

27.web: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
27.kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
27.bsb: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.

27.web: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
27.kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
27.bsb: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

27.web: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
27.kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
27.bsb: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.

27.web: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
27.kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
27.bsb: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

27.web: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
27.kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
27.bsb: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

27.web: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
27.kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
27.bsb: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

27.web: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,
27.kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them ,
27.bsb: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,

27.web: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
27.kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
27.bsb: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”

27.web: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
27.kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
27.bsb: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.

27.web: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.
27.kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
27.bsb: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.

27.web: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
27.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence , they sailed close by Crete.
27.bsb: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.

27.web: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
27.kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
27.bsb: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.

27.web: When the ship was caught, and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.
27.kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
27.bsb: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.

27.web: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
27.kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
27.bsb: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.

27.web: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
27.kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
27.bsb: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.

27.web: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
27.kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
27.bsb: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.

27.web: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
27.kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
27.bsb: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

27.web: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
27.kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us , all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
27.bsb: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.

27.web: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.
27.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
27.bsb: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.

27.web: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
27.kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
27.bsb: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.

27.web: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
27.kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
27.bsb: For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me

27.web: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
27.kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
27.bsb: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’

27.web: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
27.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
27.bsb: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.

27.web: But we must run aground on a certain island.”
27.kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
27.bsb: However, we must run aground on some island.”

27.web: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
27.kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
27.bsb: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

27.web: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
27.kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
27.bsb: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.

27.web: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.
27.kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
27.bsb: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.

27.web: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
27.kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
27.bsb: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.

27.web: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
27.kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
27.bsb: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”

27.web: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.
27.kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
27.bsb: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.

27.web: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
27.kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
27.bsb: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.

27.web: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
27.kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
27.bsb: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”

27.web: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.
27.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it , he began to eat.
27.bsb: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

27.web: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
27.kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
27.bsb: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.

27.web: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
27.kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
27.bsb: In all, there were 276 of us on board.

27.web: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
27.kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
27.bsb: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

27.web: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
27.kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
27.bsb: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

27.web: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
27.kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
27.bsb: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

27.web: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.
27.kjv: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
27.bsb: But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.

27.web: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.
27.kjv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
27.bsb: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.

27.web: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
27.kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea , and get to land:
27.bsb: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

27.web: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
27.kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
27.bsb: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.

28.web: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
28.kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
28.bsb: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

28.web: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
28.kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
28.bsb: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

28.web: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
28.kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
28.bsb: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.

28.web: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”
28.kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
28.bsb: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”

28.web: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.
28.kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
28.bsb: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

28.web: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
28.kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
28.bsb: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

28.web: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days.
28.kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
28.bsb: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.

28.web: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.
28.kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
28.bsb: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.

28.web: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured.
28.kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
28.bsb: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.

28.web: They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.
28.kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
28.bsb: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

28.web: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was “The Twin Brothers.”
28.kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
28.bsb: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.

28.web: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
28.kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
28.bsb: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

28.web: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
28.kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
28.bsb: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

28.web: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.
28.kjv: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
28.bsb: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

28.web: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.
28.kjv: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
28.bsb: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

28.web: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
28.kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
28.bsb: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

28.web: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
28.kjv: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
28.bsb: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

28.web: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.
28.kjv: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
28.bsb: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.

28.web: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.
28.kjv: But when the Jews spake against it , I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
28.bsb: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.

28.web: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”
28.kjv: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you , and to speak with you : because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
28.bsb: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”

28.web: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.
28.kjv: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
28.bsb: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.

28.web: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”
28.kjv: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
28.bsb: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”

28.web: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.
28.kjv: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
28.bsb: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.

28.web: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
28.kjv: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
28.bsb: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.

28.web: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word, “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers,
28.kjv: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
28.bsb: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:

28.web: saying, ‘Go to this people, and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.
28.kjv: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
28.bsb: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”

28.web: For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, and I would heal them.’
28.kjv: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
28.bsb: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’

28.web: “Be it known therefore to you, that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”
28.kjv: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
28.bsb: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”

28.web: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.
28.kjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

28.web: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who were coming to him,
28.kjv: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
28.bsb: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.

28.web: preaching God’s Kingdom, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
28.kjv: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
28.bsb: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
